text.p: Tropical Cyclone Harold, with 60 mph winds, is in the Coral Sea, east of Queensland, Australia, near 18s/156.0e, moving south-southeast at 7 mph. Harold is expected to continue this movement during the period. This system is mainly a risk to shipping, since it should remain well east of the Australia coast during the period.

Tropical Cyclone Karlette, with 50 mph winds, is in the Indian Ocean near 16.4s/75.9e, moving southwest at 9 mph. A turn to the west southwest is likely this period as Karlette slowly intensifies. Karlette is only a primarily a threat to shipping at this time.

Storms continue to be very strong in the northeastern Atlantic, spreading areas of strong westerly winds across northwestern Europe. This is again expected during the next few days through midweek. High seas cause problems for shipping in the North Sea and English Channel.
